narrative: Forensic Analysis: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) Fatigue Attack. On 2026-03-25, the account of a corporate administrator, 'alicia.vance@techcorp.com', was targeted. The attacker obtained the victim's primary credentials via a highly targeted spear-phishing email. When attempting to log in from an unrecognized IP address in another state (generating device fingerprint 'dev_us_8812z'), the platform's security policy triggered an automated push notification to the victim's registered mobile device. Starting at 2:45 AM local time, the attacker initiated a continuous stream of over 40 push authentication requests. Believing her phone was malfunctioning or exhausted by the constant alerts, the victim approved the notification at 3:12 AM. Once authenticated, the attacker immediately disabled future push notifications, changed the account's primary contact email, and placed an order for high-end computer hardware totaling 1,150.00 USD. The shipping address was changed to a commercial freight forwarding facility in Miami, FL. The transaction was flagged post-authorization during a routine high-risk address sweep, and the shipment was successfully intercepted.

When support requested the customer provide the drop-off receipt showing the weight of the parcel at the post office, the customer claimed they dropped it in a public post box and did not get a receipt. I did fill up my car there earlier this evening, but my actual receipt says the total was only sixty-five dollars. Why is there such a huge difference on my account?

Agent: I completely understand why that would be alarming, but I can reassure you that this is a very common practice. When you pay at the gas pump, the terminal automatically places a pre-authorization hold—usually $150—to ensure you have sufficient funds before you start dispensing fuel. Now that you've finished, the merchant will submit the actual amount of $65.00, and the remaining $85 hold will disappear.

Customer: Oh, I see! So I won't actually be charged the hundred and fifty?

Agent: Correct. The pending hold will automatically adjust to the final purchase amount of $65.00 within 24 to 48 hours, depending on how quickly the gas station processes their daily transactions. Your actual card balance is completely safe.
